title: Family & Care Legal Secretary - Nottingham
description:
Family & Care Legal Secretary - Nottingham Location: Nottingham
Salary: £25,000 per annum
Hours: Monday to Friday, 9:00am-5:00pm
Job Type: Full Time Permanent

Are you an experienced Family Legal Secretary or Care Legal Secretary looking for your next opportunity in Nottingham?

A well-established and forward-thinking law firm is looking to recruit a Legal Secretary to join its growing Family & Care department. This is an excellent opportunity to become part of a friendly, supportive team where your contribution is valued and you'll have the opportunity to develop your legal secretarial career.

The Role As a Family & Care Legal Secretary, you'll provide comprehensive secretarial and administrative support to solicitors and fee earners, helping to ensure the smooth running of the department and the delivery of excellent client care.

Your responsibilities will include:
- Providing day-to-day secretarial and administrative support to Family and Care solicitors.
- Preparing, formatting and proofreading legal documents and correspondence.
- Audio typing and accurately transcribing digital dictation.
- Opening and maintaining client files and updating legal case management systems.
- Managing diaries, arranging appointments and coordinating meetings.
- Liaising with clients, courts, counsel and other legal professionals.
- Handling telephone calls, emails and client enquiries professionally and sensitively.
- Managing incoming and outgoing correspondence.
- Assisting with general file management and departmental administration.
- Providing occasional reception cover when required.

About You Applications are welcomed from experienced Legal Secretaries, ideally with previous experience in Family Law, Childcare Law or Care Proceedings.

The successful candidate will have:
- Previous experience working as a Legal Secretary, ideally within a Family or Care department.
- Strong audio typing and legal document production skills.
- Excellent organisational skills and the ability to manage competing priorities.
- Strong attention to detail and excellent written and verbal communication skills.
- A professional, empathetic approach when dealing with clients.
- Confidence using Microsoft Office and legal case management systems.
- The ability to work independently and as part of a busy legal team.

Experience within Family or Care Law would be advantageous, although Legal Secretaries from other practice areas are also encouraged to apply.

Salary & Benefits Alongside a salary of £25,000 per annum, the firm offers an attractive benefits package, including:
- Holiday purchase scheme.
- Four additional days off over Christmas.
- Contributory pension scheme.
- Christmas bonus.
- Long-service rewards and employee referral bonuses.
- Mental health and wellbeing support.
- Free eye tests.
- Discounted conveyancing and wills services.
- Regular staff socials, team-building days and charity events.
- Employee recognition initiatives.

You'll also benefit from a modern working environment with up-to-date IT equipment, dual screens, ergonomic office furniture and comfortable staff facilities.

Why Apply? This is an excellent opportunity to join a progressive Nottingham law firm that genuinely values its employees and recognises the important contribution its legal support staff make.

You'll become part of a welcoming Family & Care team, working in a supportive environment that encourages professional development, teamwork and a healthy work-life balance.

Whether you're an experienced Family Legal Secretary, Care Legal Secretary or a Legal Secretary from another legal discipline looking for a new challenge, this could be your next career move.

Interested?

Apply today or get in touch for a confidential discussion about this Family & Care Legal Secretary opportunity in Nottingham.

title: Immigration Paralegal
description:
Role: Immigration Paralegal / Caseworker (x 2) - Nottingham

Duncan Lewis Solicitors is seeking motivated and talented Immigration Paralegals / Caseworkers to join our highly regarded Immigration Department in the City of London. This is an excellent opportunity to develop your career with one of the UK's leading law firms, recognised by The Legal 500 and Chambers & Partners as a top-tier immigration practice and awarded Law Firm of the Year at both the 2024 LexisNexis Awards and the 2023 Modern Law Awards.

Founded in 1998 and headquartered in the City of London, Duncan Lewis Solicitors is a national, award-winning, paperless law firm with over 500 professionals nationwide. With one of the UK's largest immigration law practices, we are committed to delivering exceptional legal services while staying true to our ethos: "We give people a voice."

Joining Duncan Lewis means becoming part of a diverse, supportive and forward-thinking organisation where you will have the opportunity to develop your expertise alongside some of the UK's leading immigration law specialists.

Duties and responsibilities

As an Immigration Paralegal, you will play a key role in supporting clients through a broad range of immigration matters, including both Legal Aid Agency funded and private client cases.

Key responsibilities will include:
- Reporting directly to the Department Director.
- Assisting with a wide range of immigration casework and advocacy matters.
- Meeting with clients, taking instructions, and preparing cases.
- Managing client correspondence and case communications.
- Preparing and submitting Legal Aid Agency funding applications.
- Drafting legal documents, witness statements, and supporting evidence bundles.
- Preparing immigration applications, representation letters, document indexes, and application forms to meet Home Office requirements.
- Attending client conferences, tribunals, and court hearings where appropriate.
- Maintaining accurate time recording and billing procedures.
- Implementing recommendations following file reviews and ensuring timely completion of actions.
- Ensuring compliance with file management procedures and regulatory requirements.
- Delivering outstanding client care with professionalism, empathy, and attention to detail.

Experience and qualifications

To succeed in this role, you will demonstrate a genuine passion for immigration law and a commitment to delivering exceptional client service.

Essential requirements include:
- A strong academic background with a Law degree.
- Previous experience working as an Immigration Paralegal, Caseworker, or Immigration Advisor.
- Immigration Caseworker with IAAS Level 1 accreditation desirable.
- Experience handling publicly funded immigration matters.
- Strong understanding and practical application of UK Immigration Law.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
- Strong analytical, organisational, and problem-solving abilities.
- Ability to work independently while recognising when to seek guidance.
- Professional, self-motivated, and team-oriented approach.
- Commercial awareness and the ability to promote the firm's services.
- Strong IT skills, including proficiency in Microsoft Office and document management systems.

Benefits

We offer a competitive salary and a comprehensive range of benefits designed to support your professional development, wellbeing, and work-life balance, including:
- Competitive salary with structured pay review process
- Company pension scheme
- 22 days annual leave, increasing with length of service
- Additional birthday leave
- Occupational sick pay
- Payment of practising certificate and relevant professional membership fees
- Access to extensive e-library resources and training webinars
- Employee Assistance Programme (EAP) and wellbeing support
- Employee referral scheme
- Eye care vouchers
- Enhanced family-friendly benefits
- DBS checks paid by the Company
- Flexible and hybrid working options, including part-time arrangements where appropriate
- Support for solicitor qualification and SQE1 examinations
- Clear career progression opportunities
- Support for industry recognition, awards, and professional profile development
- Company Medical Cash Plan

Subject to eligibility and Company policy.

Company culture

Duncan Lewis Solicitors is more than just a law firm. We are a nationally recognised organisation committed to excellence, diversity, and social justice.

We have been named among The Times Best Law Firms, awarded Law Firm of the Year at both the 2024 LexisNexis Awards and the 2023 Modern Law Awards, and have maintained Investors in People Gold Accreditation for over 15 years.

Our Immigration Department is recognised as a market leader, with over 160 specialist immigration lawyers nationwide handling matters ranging from business immigration and nationality applications to asylum, human rights, trafficking, and domestic abuse cases. We are proud to represent vulnerable individuals and ensure access to justice regardless of their circumstances.

At Duncan Lewis, diversity and inclusion are at the heart of everything we do. We are committed to creating an environment where all employees can thrive and where our workforce reflects the diverse communities we serve. We actively encourage applications from candidates of all backgrounds and are proud to be an Equal Opportunities employer.

Join Duncan Lewis Solicitors and become part of a firm that combines legal excellence with a genuine commitment to making a difference in people's lives.

title: Legal Secretary / Personal Assistant - Wills & Probate
description:
Legal Secretary / Personal Assistant - Wills & Probate

Location: Mansfield, Nottinghamshire

Department: Wills & Probate / Private Client

Reports to: Head of Wills & Probate

Hours: Full-time

About the Role

We are looking for an experienced Legal Secretary / Personal Assistant to provide high-quality secretarial, administrative and legal support to the Head of our Wills & Probate Department.

This role would suit an experienced Legal Secretary, Legal PA or established Paralegal with previous experience within a legal environment. Experience in Wills, Probate, Private Client or Estate Administration would be particularly advantageous.

The successful candidate will be organised, professional and confident working independently. They will need to be able to manage a busy workload, prioritise effectively and provide support with minimal supervision.

This is an experienced role and is not suitable for a new or trainee candidate requiring significant training. The successful applicant should be able to hit the ground running.

Key Responsibilities
- Providing day-to-day secretarial and PA support to the Head of Wills & Probate.
- Managing diaries, appointments, meetings and deadlines.
- Preparing and formatting correspondence, legal documents, reports and other documentation.
- Dealing with telephone calls, emails and routine client enquiries.
- Arranging client appointments and preparing relevant documentation.
- Maintaining accurate and well-organised client files and records.
- Assisting with the preparation and administration of Wills and Lasting Powers of Attorney.
- Assisting with Probate and estate administration matters.
- Preparing correspondence and documentation for review by the relevant fee earner.
- Liaising with clients, executors, beneficiaries and third parties in a professional manner.
- Liaising with organisations such as banks, building societies, HMRC and the Probate Registry where required.
- Assisting with estate administration, including obtaining information relating to assets and liabilities.
- Assisting with estate accounts and other administrative aspects of estate work.
- Monitoring outstanding work and ensuring deadlines are brought to the attention of the relevant fee earner.
- Assisting with file reviews, compliance and general case management.
- Supporting the department with billing, time recording and general administration where required.
- Maintaining confidentiality and complying with the firm's policies and procedures.
- Providing support to other members of the department when required.

Client Care

The successful candidate will have regular contact with clients, including individuals who may be dealing with bereavement or other sensitive circumstances.

It is therefore important that the successful applicant is professional, approachable, patient and empathetic, with the ability to communicate clearly and sensitively.

The candidate should be comfortable dealing with clients by telephone, email and in person and should always maintain a high standard of client service.

Experience and SkillsEssential
- Previous experience as a Legal Secretary, Legal PA, Executive Assistant or experienced Paralegal.
- Previous experience working within a legal practice.
- Excellent organisational and time-management skills.
- Strong attention to detail and accuracy.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
- Ability to manage a busy workload and competing priorities.
- Ability to work independently and use initiative.
- Good IT skills, particularly Microsoft Word and Outlook.
- Professional and confident telephone manner.
- Understanding of confidentiality and the importance of handling sensitive information.

Desirable

Experience in the following areas would be advantageous:
- Wills and Will drafting.
- Probate and estate administration.
- Private Client work.
- Lasting Powers of Attorney.
- Trusts and estate administration.
- Inheritance Tax matters.
- Estate accounts.
- Probate applications.
- Legal case management systems.

An experienced Paralegal with relevant Private Client experience will be considered, provided they have the practical experience required to undertake the role without extensive training.

Personal Qualities

We are looking for someone who is:
- Professional and approachable.
- Highly organised and methodical.
- Reliable and conscientious.
- Proactive and self-motivated.
- Discreet and trustworthy.
- Calm and professional under pressure.
- Client-focused and empathetic.
- Confident dealing with clients and third parties.
- Able to work independently as well as part of a team.
- Flexible and willing to assist colleagues when required.
- Committed to providing a high standard of work and client service.

What We Are Looking For

This position would suit an experienced legal support professional who understands the demands of working within a busy law firm and is looking for a responsible role supporting the Head of an established Wills & Probate Department.

We are particularly interested in candidates who already have experience of Wills, Probate or Private Client work and who can demonstrate a good understanding of the administrative requirements involved.

The successful candidate will be expected to work with a high degree of independence and professionalism and to become an effective member of the department quickly.

General

The duties outlined above are not exhaustive and the successful candidate may be required to undertake other reasonable duties consistent with the role and their experience.

The firm expects all employees to maintain high standards of professionalism, confidentiality, accuracy, client care and compliance with internal procedures and applicable regulatory requirements.

Please note: This is an experienced position. Candidates who are new to legal secretarial work or who require substantial training are unlikely to be suitable.

title: paralegal
description:
Job Title: Paralegal

We are seeking a motivated, organised and detail-oriented Paralegal to join a legal team. This is an excellent opportunity for someone with previous legal experience who is looking to develop their skills and progress their career within a professional legal environment.

- Preparing, drafting and reviewing legal documents and correspondence.

- Preparing bundles, schedules and supporting documentation.
- Monitoring deadlines and ensuring documents are completed and submitted on time.

- Maintaining confidentiality and delivering a professional standard of client care.

Requirements
- Previous experience working within a legal environment is desirable, with experience requirements depending on the level of the role.
- A law degree, LPC, SQE-related qualification or relevant legal experience would be advantageous.
- Good written and verbal communication skills.
- Strong organisational skills and excellent attention to detail.
- The ability to manage competing priorities and meet deadlines.
- A professional and client-focused approach.
- The ability to work independently and as part of a team.
- Good IT skills and familiarity with legal case management systems would be beneficial.

The Ideal Candidate

The ideal candidate will be proactive, reliable and enthusiastic about developing their legal career. They will have a strong work ethic, a willingness to learn and the ability to support a busy legal team effectively.

How to Apply

If you have the relevant skills and experience and are interested in developing your career within the legal sector, we would welcome your application.
